newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar says no progress made in union talks.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar says no progress made in union talks.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc said no progress was made Monday in talks with the United Auto Workers on the issue of employee firings.

"The union told us nothing today that indicates they've changed their position on the issue of employee discharges or any other matter," Wayne Zimmerman, vice president at the heavy equipment maker, said in a statement. "No progress was made and no further meetings are scheduled at this time."
The talks Monday came after Caterpillar threatened to impose employment terms at its eight U.S. plants represented by the UAW.
Employees went to work in December without a contract after a 17-month strike at Caterpillar.
A UAW spokesman was unavailable to comment on Monday's talks.
Caterpillar has said it is willing to offer arbitration for employees fired after the strike, but not those fired during or before the strike.
